newsitem.title: GERMANY: F.O. LICHT - Daily coffee report.
newsitem.headline: F.O. LICHT - Daily coffee report.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

Robusta futures in London ended narrowly firmer in quiet dealings ahead of the US long weekend. November ended $16 higher at $1,635 a tonne. There were no fresh fundamental news to give the market direction and little activity is expected on Monday when the New York arabicas market will be closed for Labour Day. However, there is still the question of scrapping the 13 per cent ICMS tax in Brazil, which could delay Brazilian shipments and lead to firmer world prices.

In New York arabica futures were slightly higher in sluggish dealings. No delivery notices were issued against the September contract. Since September entered notice period on 29 August a total of five delivery notices have been issued, as well as five stoppers. In the physical market roasters are apparently shy of paying the high premium for the spot contract. CSCE spot contract's premium to the deferreds surged as concern grew about a shortage of coffee available for delivery against September.

Certified US coffee stocks rose 4,797 bags on the week, to 39,313 the CSCE reported after the close of trading on August 26. However, spot September's open interest was still relatively high at 1,279 lots, the equivalent of about 320,000 bags of coffee.

POLAND - Poland imported 150,000 bags of coffee in March 1996, which compares to 128,496 bags imported the same month the previous year. That brought total imports since the beginning of 1996 up to 421,000 bags, 18 per cent more than was imported the same month the previous year. Total imports in calendar year 1995 rose by 6.5 per cent to 1.536 million bags.

Major suppliers of green coffee in January/March 1996 were India (65,300 vs 26,200 bags), Indonesia (82,100 vs 59,500 bags) and Vietnam (74,000 vs 79,400 bags). The country exports very little coffee and total exports in January/March 1996 were only 18,400 bags up from 11,100 bags the same period in 1995. However, total exports in calendar year 1995 rose to 42,300 bags up from 17,000 bags exported in 1994.
